ts arima¶

arima fits autoregressive integrated moving-average models by maximum likelihood: Arima for models given by their orders (p, d, q) and, optionally, seasonal orders and a seasonal period; Sarima for the same model in the usual seasonal letters (p, d, q)(P, D, Q)s.

An ARMA model explains a stationary series by its own past values and past shocks: x_t = a_1 x_{t−1} + … + a_p x_{t−p} + e_t + b_1 e_{t−1} + … + b_q e_{t−q}. The integrated part differences the series d times (and seasonally D times) first. Seasonal terms multiply the regular ones: a model with one regular and one seasonal autoregressive term of period 12 has coefficients at lags 1, 12 and 13. The likelihood is the exact Gaussian one, computed by the Kalman filter from the stationary distribution; the search is over the partial autocorrelations of each polynomial, so every candidate is stationary and invertible.

The Surface¶

Entity

What it gives you

Arima

Fits an ARIMA model by maximum likelihood

ArimaFit

The result of an ARIMA fit: the estimated coefficients and the methods that evaluate the fitted model

ArimaOptions

Options of ts::Arima::fit_mle: the orders of the model, starting values and search settings

Sarima

Fits a seasonal ARIMA model by maximum likelihood, in the notation (p, d, q)(P, D, Q)s

SarimaFit

The result of a seasonal ARIMA fit: an ArimaFit plus the orders it was fitted with

SarimaOptions

Options of ts::Sarima::fit_mle: the orders in the usual seasonal letters

How To Call It¶

Fit an AR(1) model to an autoregressive series, compare it with a moving-average model by log-likelihood, and forecast three steps.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = ar1(200, 0.7);
  ts::ArimaOptions options;
  options.ar_order = 1;
  const auto fit = ts::Arima::fit_mle(y, options);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "AR(1) coefficient " << fit.ar[0] << ", innovation sd " << fit.sigma << ", log-likelihood " << fit.loglik(y) << "\n";

  ts::ArimaOptions ma;
  ma.ar_order = 0;
  ma.ma_order = 1;
  std::cout << "MA(1) log-likelihood " << ts::Arima::fit_mle(y, ma).loglik(y) << "\n";
  show("forecast", fit.forecast(3, y));
}

Output

AR(1) coefficient 0.6506, innovation sd 0.2841, log-likelihood -32.3468
MA(1) log-likelihood -45.3373
forecast         0.2706   0.1929   0.1423
